summary: The team is pivoting promotion decisively toward China-based programs — Asia Star and Intelligent China — while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and clearing a cluster of near-term content and event deliverables.
summaryDetail: The strategic priority right now is the China-program push: Asia Star and Intelligent China lead promotion, with the Berkeley program a possible third, while US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) are on hold for Q1 — so Joseph's targeting document and the Google Analytics conversion-tracking brief and validation are the gating items to get measurement right before spend ramps. The Knowledge website redesign is close to settled: keep the current design with menu-categorization improvements, drop the standalone videos section in favor of topic-based dispersal, fold in BCI/BSI indices, and use Joseph's editorial layout as inspiration — Joseph's HTML file, a 30-minute feedback-marking session, and Joker's design changes are the immediate follow-through. Several dated deliverables need attention this week: Julie's 24th-anniversary social post (Nov 21) using the Blue Carrot video, Xuan's final read on the Nov 13 event summary (shorter WeChat version with Prof Tao's original feedback), Kaylee's polite decline to Niamh Dawson over the WIL Forum recording clauses, and Ira/Julie's feedback on the new Knowledge site before next Tuesday. Also pending: the YouTube channel improvement plan and moderator brief reviews, Jen's forwarding of video links and LinkedIn posts to Andrea and Katja, and WEPs China Forum registration by Nov 20 — with the Outlook lockout a resolved-but-not-closed housekeeping item (confirm JSB backend unlock and update all devices).

decisions.text: Stale saved credentials on devices caused repeated failed logins and account lockout; all devices must be updated.
Keep the current Knowledge design largely as-is, with menu categorization as the main improvement.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic instead.
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Use Joseph's editorial-style layout as inspiration to display more articles, not to follow exactly.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for promotion, with Berkeley program as a potential third priority.
